1. LEFT: BR 18→15, yellow 45→36 (erased another 9). So the piece can keep erasing while moving! The earlier stop was... wait, earlier after 11 LEFTs it stopped at 18. Now LEFT works (18→15). Hmm, actually maybe it moved 8 times and the 9th-11th were blocked... but now LEFT works. What changed?
2. RIGHT: BR 15→18, yellow 36→45 — the yellow was restored! So erasure is reversible: moving back restores the yellow. The yellow isn't destroyed, it's a "ghost" — the piece's overlap hides the yellow, and the yellow reappears when the piece moves away. So the yellow is just an obstacle that the piece can partially overlap (up to some limit?).
3. UP: BR 42→39 (moved up 3), yellow fully restored to 54 [42,47,9,20]!
So the "erasure" is just visual overlap. The piece can overlap the yellow. Then why did it stop at 18 after 11 LEFTs? And why did the subsequent LEFT (18→15) work?
Hmm wait — maybe the piece stops when the overlap exceeds some threshold... at 18: overlap = bar cols 18-20 (9 cells). At 15: overlap = bar 15-20 (18 cells) + stub? BR's stub at 18-23... at 15: stub cols 18-23, yellow's stub 12-17 → no overlap. So at 15, overlap = 18 cells.
Why did it stop at 18 after 11 LEFTs? Maybe... the 9th LEFT was blocked by something else? At that time BR was at 18-29. 9th LEFT → 15-26. Overlap with yellow (then 45, cols 9-17): bar 15-17 (9 cells). Should be fine...
Oh wait. Maybe the piece can't move if the move would cause the yellow piece to become disconnected! At 18: yellow = bar 9-17 + stub 12-17 (connected). 9th LEFT → 15: yellow = bar 9-14 + stub 12-17 → still connected. Hmm, no.
Or: the piece stops when the overlap would cause the yellow's bounding box to shrink below some minimum?
Or: the earlier stop was a one-off thing — maybe the piece was "stuck" because the yellow's bar was 9 wide (cols 9-17), and the piece's bar (12 wide) at 15-26 would... no.
Let me test more: LEFT again (15→12?), LEFT, LEFT... see where it stops. If it keeps erasing, then the earlier stop was temporary (maybe the piece can't make 3 consecutive moves into the same yellow? or a cooldown?).
Actually! Maybe the rule is: the piece can't move if the current position already overlaps the yellow (must first move away)? But the LEFT from 18 (overlapping) to 15 worked. Contradiction.
Hmm, wait, let me re-check: after 11 LEFTs, BR was at 18-29, yellow was 45. Then LEFT → 15-26, yellow 36. Then RIGHT → 18-29, yellow 45. Then UP → 39-44, yellow 54.
So movement while overlapping works in both directions. Then why did the 9th-11th LEFTs in the batch stop at 18?
Oh. Maybe the batched LEFTs: each action moves 3 cols, but maybe the piece moves 3 cols per action only if there's no overlap, and moves less if there's overlap? No...
Or: the 9th LEFT was blocked because at that moment the yellow was 45 (bar 9-17, stub 12-17), and BR at 15-26: BR's bar rows 42-44 cols 15-26 overlaps yellow's bar 15-17; BR's stub rows 45-47 cols 18-23 vs yellow's stub 12-17: no overlap. No issue.
I'm confused. Let me test: from current position (BR at 39-44, 18-29, above the yellow), move DOWN (39→42, re-overlap by 9), then LEFT, LEFT, LEFT and observe.
Actually, a simpler hypothesis: the piece can overlap the yellow, but the piece's move is blocked if the destination overlaps the yellow by more than 9 cells (3 cols)? At 15: overlap = 18 cells (bar 15-20). That worked. So no.
Let me look at the image: BR is now at rows 39-44, cols 18-29, above the yellow Yl' (42-47, 9-20). The yellow is fully restored (54).
New idea: maybe the earlier stop was because the piece was trying to move into a position where the yellow's remaining part (45) would be disconnected from...? No.
Let me re-examine the sequence more carefully. After 5 DOWNs: BR at 42-47, 42-53. Then 11 LEFTs. Observed final: 18-29. That's 8 moves (24 cols). If all 11 had executed: 42-33=9 → cols 9-20 = exact match with yellow. It stopped at 18.
Hypothesis: the piece stops when the overlap would cause the yellow to be completely covered? At 15: yellow's bar 9-14 + stub 12-17 remain — not covered. At 9: exact match — yellow fully covered. Maybe the piece is blocked from fully covering the yellow?? At 15-26, yellow's bar 9-14 (6) + stub 12-17 (6) = 36 remain. Not fully covered.
Hmm, what's special about 18? At 18-29: overlap 9. At 15-26: overlap 18. Both allowed (18→15 worked).
Wait, maybe the stop at 18 was because the yellow was 54 (full) at that time? No — the yellow was 45 when it stopped (I observed 45 after the batch).
Let me re-verify: after the batch, state showed Y 45 [42,47,9,17], B 48 [42,47,18,29]. So it stopped at 18 with the yellow at 45. Then a single LEFT → 15, yellow 36.
The difference: batched vs single? Maybe in a batch, the piece processes one move per frame and stops when blocked... but it wasn't blocked (the single LEFT worked).
Or: the piece can't move while overlapping the yellow if the move direction would increase the overlap... but 18→15 increased the overlap (9→18).
I'm going in circles. Empirically: let me test a batch of LEFTs from a clean position.
Current: BR at 39-44, 18-29 (above the yellow). Plan: DOWN (→42-47, overlap 9), then LEFT×3 in a batch, observe.
Actually, let me think about what the goal is. The yellow is restorable — so the goal is probably: fully cover the yellow (exact match) → level clear (yellow disappears). The piece can overlap the yellow. To fully cover Yl' (54) with BR (54): exact match at cols 9-20, rows 42-47. BR is currently at 39-44, 18-29. Needed: DOWN (→42), LEFT×3 (→9).
But the earlier batch stopped at 18... let me test LEFT×3 as a batch after DOWN and see if it reaches 9.
